profiles.rationale: The explicit 16-feature closure was exercised in a generic in-process host with durable runtime persistence, resumption, trigger scheduling and the deployable local filesystem lock provider. This is a starting selection: the persistence resource, connection, lock directory, signing and migration choices remain host-owned. Runtime API is included and can expose endpoints when a web host maps it.
profiles.title: Embedded runtime
profiles.description: Run and resume workflows inside your process using a durable runtime store and local filesystem locking. Review the Runtime API feature and supply host-specific prerequisites separately.

dependencyExplanations.reason: The Runtime API feature registers its routes through API capabilities.
Durable runtime persistence requires the workflow resumption feature.
Runtime resumption schedules its pump through the Tasks feature.
Runtime trigger endpoints are supplied by the Runtime API feature.

profiles.rationale: This 19-feature Worker starting selection adds provider-agnostic identity contracts, OIDC bearer integration, and a separate Identity IAM EF persistence target to the explicit 16-feature embedded runtime selection. Authority, Audience, provider and tenant identifiers, normalization, Runtime and IAM resources and connections, migration policy, lock and signing inputs remain host-owned. Selecting the profile neither provisions schemas nor enrolls IAM in the Runtime store. Runtime API endpoints remain subject to host route mapping; deployments require HTTPS metadata.
profiles.title: Worker HTTP
profiles.description: Start an HTTP worker with durable workflow runtime features, bearer authentication, and a separate Identity IAM persistence target. Configure host-owned identity, Runtime, IAM, locking, signing, and migration settings separately.

groups.rationale: Select API capability aggregation, the two server diagnostics features and their EF persistence consumers together. The two consumers still need independently reviewed resource bindings, migration policy, and host prerequisites; this group does not configure or validate a database or enable in-process engine tracing.
groups.title: Diagnostics with EF persistence
groups.description: Add Structured Logs and OpenTelemetry diagnostic stores to a server composition. Configure each EF consumer and its database resource separately.

dependencyExplanations.reason: The diagnostics feature contributes its management contract through API capability aggregation.
The OpenTelemetry EF persistence consumer depends on the OpenTelemetry diagnostics feature.
The diagnostics feature contributes its management contract through API capability aggregation.
The Structured Logs EF persistence consumer depends on the Structured Logs diagnostics feature.
